text_blocks.snippet: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) treatment focuses on managing symptoms and slowing lung damage, as there's no cure. Augmentation therapy, which involves weekly intravenous infusions of purified AAT protein from donors, is a key treatment to raise AAT levels in the lungs and potentially slow disease progression. Other treatments include managing symptoms like those of COPD (bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids) and addressing liver issues. Importantly, lifestyle modifications like quitting smoking are crucial for managing AATD.
snippet_highlighted_words: focuses on managing symptoms and slowing lung damage

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: This treatment involves infusing AAT protein, derived from healthy donors, into the bloodstream.

list.title: Goal:
list.snippet: To increase the level of AAT in the lungs, thereby providing protection against the destructive effects of neutrophil elastase.

list.title: Effectiveness:
list.snippet: While it doesn't reverse existing lung damage, it can slow the progression of lung disease in individuals with AATD.

list.title: Administration:
list.snippet: Typically given weekly through intravenous infusion.

list.title: Considerations:
list.snippet: It's a lifelong treatment and may have mild side effects like headache, muscle aches, or flu-like symptoms.
Bronchodilators and Inhaled Corticosteroids: Similar to treatments for COPD, these medications help to open up airways and reduce inflammation in the lungs.
Pulmonary Rehabilitation: This program includes exercise, breathing techniques, and education to improve lung function and overall health.
Oxygen Therapy: May be needed for individuals with low oxygen levels.
Lung Transplantation: Considered for severe lung damage.
Liver Transplant: May be necessary for severe liver disease caused by AATD.
Quitting Smoking: Essential to prevent further lung damage.
Avoiding Environmental Irritants: This includes secondhand smoke, dust, and air pollution.
Healthy Diet: May involve eating plenty of fruits and vegetables, choosing healthy proteins, and getting enough vitamin D and phosphorus, according to the Alpha-1 Foundation.

list.title: Early Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Early detection of AATD is crucial to initiate treatment and potentially slow disease progression.

list.title: Multidisciplinary Approach:
list.snippet: Managing AATD often involves a team of healthcare professionals, including pulmonologists, hepatologists, and genetic counselors.

list.title: Ongoing Research:
list.snippet: Research is ongoing to find new and improved treatments for AATD, including gene therapy.
